title: Prevent concurrent writers to same RAM buffer
description: When one Record instance is already recording to a shared RAM buffer (R1-R4), a second Record instance can start recording to that same buffer. The second start clears the buffer and both instances can then write concurrently, causing nondeterministic/interleaved results based on host processing order.
acceptance_criteria:
- Starting recording on channel Ri while another instance is already recording channel Ri is deterministic and safe (single-writer semantics).
- Existing recording on Ri is not silently clobbered by another instance's NoteOn.
- Behavior is explicitly defined (ignore second trigger, steal with explicit policy, or reject with state flag) and covered by tests.
- Cross-instance tests verify no concurrent-write race on the same channel.
- cargo fmt --check passes.
- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passes.
- cargo test passes.
close_reason: Implemented generation counters for per-channel recording ownership. When a new instance starts recording on a channel, it bumps the generation; the previous writer detects the mismatch and stops. Most-recent-write-wins policy with deterministic single-writer semantics.

title: Calibrate sampler character against Machinedrum UW captures
description: Partial sound match, not complete emulation. Firmware and disposable-RAM1 measurements replaced community timing approximations in Ultrawave-mdtiming; RTIM0 is fastest, not OFF. Six analog sweeps, pitched playback, three internal generations, silence-overwrite control and checksum-verified read-only RAM1 SDS exports now separate capture from playback. External capture is nearly flat (+0.10/+0.03/-0.29 dB at 8/16/19 kHz relative 1 kHz); playback loses 1.70/5.14/7.98 dB and remains pitch-dependent. Internal generation adds 3.25/12.86/21.22 dB. This disproves the fitted steep capture-filter hypothesis. Only a conventional normalized 17 Hz wet high-pass is implemented: repeated 30 Hz loss is about 1.13 dB; filter once before output/feedback split, continuous across voices, reset by host. Dry/external capture unchanged. Independent f64 oracles, Linux full loop, native Mac tests and real Renoise 16/16 plus REAPER pass. Remaining: separate interpolation, always-running track processing and internal main tap before choosing a small causal treble model; verify native clock, quantizer encoding, BRR/SRR, drive/envelopes and held-out level-matched drums/tones. SDS occupies all low-nibble codes, so plain shifted 12-bit PCM is unproven. Do not implement guessed host-rate averaging FIR or apply analog coloration to each internal generation. Held-out 17/60/200/1000 Hz/drum acquisition stopped before mutation because PipeWire owns Scarlett playback; do not interrupt unrelated audio sessions. Interface loopback is optional, Scarlett provisionally flat. Resume only with exclusive access and permitted RAM1, snapshot/restore Kit/Global/routes, switch Scarlett 3/4 from Mix C/D to PCM 3/4 before sends or physical loopback. All completed acquisitions restored controls/routes; RAM1 contents were authorized disposable. See docs/testing/machinedrum-measurement.md and machinedrum-whitepaper.md, including corrected OS1.53 revJ manual attribution and private evidence paths. No verified whitepaper sampler filter was found in silver-release.

title: Correct retrigger timing, disabled interval and infinite-count semantics
description: Investigation found four correctness gaps. Official Elektron OS1.63 manual A15 specifies RTRG127 infinite and RTIM tempo-relative, with RTIM0 disabling RTRG; A16 says RAM Play matches ROM25-48. Current RamPlay uses finite counts including 127, linear 0-500ms intervals independent of host tempo, and increments the counter before rendering the initial sample.
